PSALM 57

. Altaschith--or, "Destroy not." This is perhaps an enigmatical allusion to the critical circumstances connected with the history, for which compare ; . In Moses' prayer () it is a prominent petition deprecating God's anger against the people. This explanation suits the fifty-eighth and fifty-ninth also. Asaph uses it for the seventy-fifth, in the scope of which there is allusion to some emergency. Michtam--(See on , title). To an earnest cry for divine aid, the Psalmist adds, as often, the language of praise, in the assured hope of a favorable hearing.

1. my soul--or self, or life, which is threatened.

shadow of thy wings--(; ).

calamities--literally, "mischiefs" (; ).
2. performeth--or, completes what He has begun.

3. from ... swallow me up--that pants in rage after me ().

mercy and ... truth--(; ), as messengers () sent to deliver him.

4. The mingled figures of wild beasts (; ) and weapons of war () heighten the picture of danger.

whose ... tongue--or slanders.
5. This doxology illustrates his view of the connection of his deliverance with God's glory.
6. (Compare ; , ).
7. I will ... praise--both with voice and instrument.

8. Hence--he addresses his glory, or tongue (; ), and his psaltery, or lute, and harp.

I myself ... early--literally, "I will awaken dawn," poetically expressing his zeal and diligence.
9-10. As His mercy and truth, so shall His praise, fill the universe.
